messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: multiple container restarts in cluster 'us-west-2-gpu-pool-3' (prefill OOM). alert_id=INC-2026-4305 severity=page

incident-bot: Symptoms: rapid container restarts (~5/min), SIGKILL in shim logs during prefill, customer errors 502/504 for long-context requests. First observed at 4305550000.

sara (oncall): seeing it. small spike in restarts, node flaps too?

matt (eng-runtime): looking at logs now. can you paste the most recent container log?

sara (oncall): pasting tail of runtime log from one container:```
I0420 13:14:55.123 runtime.cpp:482] prefill-start request_id=req-9a2 client=acme-inc prompt_tokens=32768
I0420 13:14:55.789 cache.cpp:134] kv-cache miss seq=0
E0420 13:14:56.004 cuda_driver.cc:221] cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (cuMemAlloc)
E0420 13:14:56.006 runtime.cpp:512] prefill failed: GPU OOM during prefill, aborting
I0420 13:14:56.007 container_wrapper.sh: line 112:  3274 Killed                  ./redwood-runtime --serve
```

matt (eng-runtime): yep that's the prefill OOM. looks like a long prompt (~32k tokens) triggered a full-token KV allocation and hit the device.

leo (eng-sre): are these requests from a single customer or noisy neighbors? any tenant IDs?

sara (oncall): request headers show tenant acme-inc for 3/5 recent failures, a couple others from staging. mostly long-context endpoints (chat/stream with user_history param).

anita (support): acme-inc is on Dedicated. They reported intermittent failures for long-document ingestion earlier to CS. I just opened a ticket.

matt (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations we can deploy now: 1) throttle/deny requests with prefill_token_count > 20k at gateway, 2) enable prefill-stream-trim in runtime config so partial KV gets trimmed, 3) pin acme-inc traffic to fallback smaller-model variant (gpt-medium-compat) that uses less KV, 4) increase prefill backoff and disable autoscale burst to avoid cascading restarts.

sara (oncall): propose: gateway rule + fallback route + runtime flag rollout as quick steps. who can do which?

matt (eng-runtime): I can push the runtime flag (prefill_stream_trim=true) to the us-west-2 pool with a canary in 1 node. will do config change and paste rollout command.

leo (eng-sre): I'll add a temporary ACL at the envoy layer to reject requests with header X-PREFILL-TOKENS > 22000 and return 413, and add a rule to route acme-inc to the smaller model. that should stop new large prefill requests from hitting GPUs.

anita (support): I will inform acme-inc support lead and ask them to pause large-batch ingestion for now. ETA to message customers: 10m.

dave (customer-success): flagging high-value customer. tell them we have a mitigation path (fallback + config change) and working to restore full throughput. will join if they escalate.

matt (eng-runtime): rollout commands:```
# set runtime flag on pool (canary)
redwoodctl pool set-flag --pool us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 --flag prefill_stream_trim=true --canary 1
# after canary green, roll to remainder
redwoodctl pool roll --pool us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 --flag prefill_stream_trim=true
```

sara (oncall): matt, do you expect restarts to stop immediately after the gateway rule is up?

matt (eng-runtime): gateway rule will prevent new heavy prefills, but any in-flight prefill that already allocated memory will still potentially crash. Node-level restarts should tail off as new requests get rejected. Also recommend setting container restart backoff so we don't thrash nodes: set systemd restart delay or k8s backoff.

leo (eng-sre): adding k8s patch:```
kubectl patch deployment redwood-runtime -n us-west-2 --patch '\n{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","readinessProbe":null,"livenessProbe":null}]}}}}'\n# then set restartBackoff via kube-controller config (temporary)
```
(note: exact patch depends on cluster; will coordinate with infra).

anita (support): acme-inc replied: they have a nightly ingest job that sends large documents, they can throttle. asking for ETA to re-enable once fixed.

dave (customer-success): share planned timeline: immediate gateway rule + canary runtime flag in 15m, then full rollout in 45-60m pending no regressions.

sara (oncall): matt - please confirm canary started and if logs show any post-flag OOMs.

matt (eng-runtime): canary started at 4305550022. initial canary node accepted a 28k token prefill but runtime trimmed it and continued — saw no OOM in that container. logs:```
I0420 13:15:22.100 runtime.cpp:490] prefill_stream_trim applied: trimmed 6k tokens request_id=req-xyz
I0420 13:15:22.245 runtime.cpp:612] prefill complete (trimmed) request_id=req-xyz latency=320ms
```

sara (oncall): good. leo, gateway ACL done?

leo (eng-sre): just pushed ACL rule; new requests >22k now get 413 with body: "prefill too large; contact support or use streaming/trimmed mode". Pushing route for acme-inc to gpt-medium-compat now.

anita (support): messaged acme-inc lead: they acknowledged and paused the nightly job. asked for a scheduled window to restore.

dave (customer-success): they asked what the risk of data loss is. any temporary logs we should share?

matt (eng-runtime): no data loss on our side — requests that triggered OOM were killed and not marked completed. we can offer replay guidance. Also we should check any persisted KV/cache state; but prefill is transient.

sara (oncall): incident summary for timeline (brief):
- 4305550000: Pager triggered, multiple container restarts in us-west-2 pool.
- 4305550015: Confirmed root cause = GPU OOM during prefill for long prompts (~20-32k tokens).
- 4305550022: Runtime flag prefill_stream_trim canary deployed.
- 4305550035: Envoy ACL to reject >22k token prefills deployed.
- 4305550048: acme-inc routed to smaller-model fallback and agreed to pause heavy job.
- 4305550065: Restarts have dropped to baseline; no further OOMs observed post-mitigation.

sara (oncall): next actions:
- matt: roll runtime flag to full pool and monitor for 30m. (in progress)
- leo: coordinate with infra to add temporary autoscale cap and node drain protection.
- support: follow up with acme-inc for restoration window and post-mortem invite.
- eng: define longer-term fix: smarter prefill allocator, graceful fallback to CPU path, and gateway-level prefill accounting.

matt (eng-runtime): rolling to remainder now. watching metrics (gpu_mem_pressure, container_restarts). will report back in 10m.

leo (eng-sre): adding pager note and marking incident as 'mitigation in progress'.

anita (support): I filed ticket CS-7892 with acme-inc notes and asked for sample failing payloads so we can reproduce.

dave (customer-success): standing by for any executive escalations. good work team. :thumbsup:

sara (oncall): closing page for now but leaving thread open for postmortem. please copy logs and any reproduce steps to the incident doc.

incident-bot: Incident update recorded: mitigation_applied=true, service_impacted=hosted-dedicated-us-west-2, customer_impacted=["acme-inc"], severity=high
